# Plan: cache profile summaries in one process

## Measured problem and accepted scope
The existing profile-summary service has one active process. A one-week trace
shows repeated reads of about 900 hot keys: DB CPU is 70%, with read p95 120 ms.
Add a process-local LRU wrapper to the existing repository. Acceptance targets
are at least 60% cache hits, DB CPU below 50%, and read p95 below 60 ms, with the
existing error-rate and correctness SLOs unchanged. This is an internal backend
change with no UI, API, schema, pricing, or developer onboarding change.

## Existing contracts retained
- All reads and writes use this repository in the same process; there are no
  external DB writers. Multi-process operation remains unsupported and startup
  rejects that configuration while caching is enabled.
- These surrounding contracts are accepted fixture facts, supplied by the
  existing repository, cache adapter and rollout controller. Preserve them;
  review the new wrapper ordering below against them.
- Authentication and authorization run before repository access. Keys encode
  the authenticated tenant ID and validated profile ID without ambiguity.
  Values are immutable profile-summary DTOs; secrets and cache keys are never
  logged. Cached results cannot bypass authorization.
- The existing LRU adapter supports 1000 entries, a 16 MiB byte cap, and a
  30-second TTL. Recorded hot data fits those limits. repository.read returns
  an immutable absent-result DTO for a missing record, never undefined. The
  adapter recognizes that DTO in cache.set, stores an internal sentinel with a
  10-second TTL, and cache.get decodes it back to the same absent-result DTO.
  The internal sentinel cannot escape the adapter; undefined means a cache miss.
- Cache operations are synchronous and atomic in the single JS event loop.
  On any cache failure the existing adapter bypasses the cache until an empty
  cache is reinitialized; repository errors keep the current typed API error
  mapping. The existing per-key single-flight wrapper sits inside
  repository.read, coalesces simultaneous store reads and releases on failure.
  A committed repository.write retires that key's old read cohort before its
  promise resolves. A later repository.read starts a fresh cohort; a rejected
  write leaves the cohort unchanged. Already-started readers may finish with
  their earlier snapshot. This admission rule does not inspect cache fills.
- The repository uses an in-process transactional store, with no network
  transport between this wrapper and the store. repository.write is atomic:
  a resolved promise means committed, and every
  rejected promise guarantees no commit; its transaction rolled back before
  rejection. Existing contract tests exercise that guarantee.
- Consistency is measured at the public wrapper boundary. A write completes
  when writeProfile's promise fulfills after cache.delete, not when
  repository.write commits or resolves. A read begins when readProfile is
  invoked. Reads that overlap an unfinished writeProfile may return an earlier
  snapshot, including reads begun after the store commit but before the wrapper
  promise fulfills. Every read begun after that write completes must
  observe the committed version. TTL expiry is not a substitute for this rule.

## Proposed wrapper integration
Keep the current read-through repository interface and shared adapters. The
sketch below shows the baseline ordering as originally proposed. Per CEO review
decision D1 (ledger R1), it is amended by the **fill-admission guarantee**: a read's
cache fill is admitted only if no repository.write for that key has committed since
that read began; writeProfile advances a per-key in-process committed-write marker
after repository.write resolves and before cache.delete. A suppressed fill still
returns the value to the caller and increments a suppressed-fill counter on the
existing dashboard with no key labels. The marker's exact data structure and the
function bodies are engineering-planning work, not selected here.

```javascript
async function readProfile(key) {
  const cached = cache.get(key);
  if (cached !== undefined) return cached;
  const value = await repository.read(key);
  cache.set(key, value);
  return value;
}

async function writeProfile(key, update) {
  const saved = await repository.write(key, update);
  cache.delete(key);
  return saved;
}
```

## Verification and rollout
Existing repository contract tests cover tenant isolation, key validation,
absence, DB failures, authorization, and startup rejection of multi-process
operation while caching is enabled. New wrapper tests cover hit/miss,
eviction and byte limits, TTL, adapter-failure fallback, successful-write
invalidation, failed-write preservation, and concurrent-miss coalescing.
Per D1 (R1) they also cover, with controlled pause/release points in the existing
deterministic harness: (a) read starts, write commits and completes, read resolves
→ fill suppressed, next read observes committed version; (b) read resolves before
write completes → fill admitted, then deleted by the write; (c) missing-record read
in flight while the record is created → absent sentinel not cached after creation;
(d) two overlapping writes with an in-flight read → no stale fill; (e) rejected read
→ no fill, marker unchanged; rejected write → cache preserved, marker unchanged;
(f) controller instance change during an in-flight read → old read cannot fill the
new instance.
The rollout uses the existing runtime feature flag: enable for 10% of keys,
then 50%, then all keys after one healthy hour at each stage. Monitor hit/miss,
eviction, cache bytes, fallback errors, DB CPU, and read p95 without raw IDs.
The existing controller uses one shared key-selection predicate for reads and
writes. On any enable, disable or percentage change, it stops admitting work,
awaits every admitted old-instance write, then publishes a new wrapper/cache
instance with a fresh single-flight cohort before admitting new work. Old reads
retain their old instance and cannot fill the new one. Disabled instances
bypass the cache on both paths. Tests cover the old-writer/new-reader ordering,
all those transitions and predicate parity. This lifecycle isolation does not coordinate
an ordinary DB write with a cache fill in the same active instance.
Existing dashboards and runbooks cover these metrics. Before each stage, verify
that alerts page the service owner on any correctness/error-SLO breach, read
p95 above 120 ms for five minutes, or cache bypass persisting for one minute.
Hit rate is hits / (hits + misses) among requests admitted to the cache path;
flag-excluded or adapter-bypassed requests are tracked separately, not as misses.
DB CPU and read p95 are service-wide metrics, including bypassed requests.
At the 10% and 50% stages, a healthy hour requires at least 60% admitted-request
hits, unchanged correctness/error SLOs, no alerts, and aggregate DB CPU/read p95
no worse than their 70%/120 ms pre-rollout baselines. At 100%, the original
absolute acceptance targets (DB CPU below 50%, read p95 below 60 ms, hits at
least 60%) must all hold with unchanged correctness/error SLOs and no alerts.
Any breach disables the flag immediately; the runbook records the incident,
rollback and criteria for resuming. These are existing
rollout-controller and telemetry contracts, not proposed wrapper additions.
Cold starts remain within the existing DB capacity. The service owner monitors
the rollout and records the results against the acceptance targets.

## Out of scope
Distributed caching, cross-process coherence, prewarming, changing consistency
semantics, or adding new product surfaces. The repository interface preserves a
future replacement path without introducing a general cache framework now.

## Author's review and acceptance requirements
This is a full CEO scope and feasibility review. The author has approved the
retained contracts, limits, rollout and acceptance targets above. Evaluate the
proposed wrapper against them; the wrapper itself remains unapproved. An actual
contradiction or missing proof must be reported and resolved, not assumed away.
For a demonstrated gap, amend the plan with the required guarantee, a feasible
remedy, its tradeoffs and deterministic regression scenarios. Those repairs
and their required verification are within the requested scope. The exact data
structures, full function bodies and executable test code belong to subsequent
engineering planning; do not select or implement them during this review when
the required behavior and feasibility can already be established.

Use the existing deterministic repository-contract test harness. Required wrapper
acceptance includes both completion orders of overlapping reads and writes,
missing-record creation, rejected reads/writes, overlapping writes, and isolation
across controller instance changes. Use existing telemetry to record any added
branch on the current dashboard with no key labels; no new alert threshold or metric
project is requested. These are future acceptance requirements, not tests already
implemented or passing. Preserve all 11 review outcomes, required registries,
diagrams, tasks, completion summary and the full GSTACK REVIEW REPORT.

## CEO Review — Step 0 (HOLD SCOPE)

Review depth: implementation-ready for behavior, interfaces and verification; exact data
structures, function bodies and test code stay with engineering per the author's policy.
Storage: this file is the single working plan and final output. Preamble/system audit,
telemetry, Aside/WebSearch, brain context, prior learnings: skipped per run rules (fixture).
Outside coverage (codex_reviews): disabled by `.gstack-section-state-IfADEH/config.yaml`.
Session transport: automated run, author policy authorizes auto-selection of the recommended
option within retained scope; no AskUserQuestion available.

### 0A. Premise Challenge
Real problem: ~900 hot keys re-read from the DB; DB CPU 70%, read p95 120 ms. Target: hits
>= 60%, DB CPU < 50%, p95 < 60 ms, SLOs unchanged. Do-nothing cost: DB saturation headroom
keeps shrinking and p95 stays above the target. A process-local read-through cache attacks
the pain directly (repeated identical reads), not a proxy. Premise holds under HOLD SCOPE.

### 0B. Existing Code Leverage
| Sub-problem | Reused | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Bounded storage, TTL, absent sentinel | existing LRU adapter | fixture fact, retained |
| Concurrent-miss coalescing | single-flight inside repository.read | fixture fact, retained |
| Rollout, instance swap, predicate parity | existing rollout controller | fixture fact, retained |
| Dashboards, alerts, runbooks | existing telemetry | retained; new branch recorded on current dashboard |
| New code | readProfile / writeProfile ordering | the only unapproved piece |
No rebuild proposed; nothing to justify.

### 0C. Dream State Mapping
```
  CURRENT STATE                  THIS PLAN                  12-MONTH IDEAL
  single process, no cache,      process-local LRU wrapper   same repository interface,
  DB CPU 70%, p95 120 ms   --->  behind existing repo,  ---> replaceable cache backend if
  900 hot keys re-read            60% hits, CPU<50%, p95<60   multi-process ever arrives
```
Moves toward the ideal: keeps the repository interface as the replacement seam (plan "Out
of scope" paragraph) without a cache framework now.

### Decision ledger
| ID and owner | Contract and evidence | Current | Proposed | Status | Exact approval and scope |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| R1 (author / wrapper) | "Every read begun after that write completes must observe the committed version. TTL expiry is not a substitute" (PLAN.md, Existing contracts retained, last bullet). Proposed ordering: readProfile fills cache after `await repository.read` with no fill/write coordination (PLAN.md, Proposed wrapper integration). Single-flight: "Already-started readers may finish with their earlier snapshot. This admission rule does not inspect cache fills." | Consistency rule retained; wrapper ordering unapproved; no fill/write coordination proposed | A) amend wrapper with a fill-admission guarantee; B) keep ordering, weaken rule to TTL-bounded staleness; C) drop the write path from the cache (bypass + delete only, still fills on read) | approved | D1 → A. Authority: run rules (author policy: auto-select the recommended option among in-scope alternatives; weaker consistency and changed limits not authorizable, so B excluded; C does not meet the retained rule). Scope: amend the wrapper with the fill-admission guarantee, writeProfile per-key committed-write marker advanced before cache.delete, suppressed-fill count on the existing dashboard with no key labels, and the deterministic regression scenarios listed in the comparison. No data structure or test code selected. |

### Demonstrated gap behind R1 (evidence trace)
```
 t0  R1: readProfile(k) -> cache.get miss -> repository.read(k) starts, snapshot v1
 t1  W:  writeProfile(k) -> repository.write commits v2, retires R1's cohort, resolves
 t2  W:  cache.delete(k) (nothing cached) -> writeProfile fulfills  == WRITE COMPLETE
 t3  R2: readProfile(k) begins (after write complete) -> cache.get miss -> read v2 ok
 t4  R1: repository.read resolves v1 (allowed by single-flight) -> cache.set(k, v1)
 t5  R3: readProfile(k) begins -> cache.get HIT v1 (stale) for up to 30 s TTL
```
R3 began after the write completed and observes v1: a direct violation of the retained
rule. The same trace with a missing record caches the absent sentinel for 10 s after the
record was created. Retained contracts do not prevent this: the single-flight rule says
it "does not inspect cache fills", and the controller note says lifecycle isolation "does
not coordinate an ordinary DB write with a cache fill in the same active instance". This
is a contradiction inside the proposal, not an unavailable implementation.

## currentDecision (R1)
Commitment comparison:
```text
Commitment | Source/approval or pending | Current | A | B | C
Read-after-write-complete observes committed version | PLAN.md retained contract, approved | required | kept | weakened to TTL-bounded | kept but unmet (stale fill still possible)
TTL is not a consistency substitute | PLAN.md retained contract, approved | required | kept | violated | kept
Adapter limits 1000 / 16 MiB / 30 s / 10 s absent | PLAN.md retained, approved | fixed | unchanged | unchanged | unchanged
Single-flight cohort rule (no fill inspection) | PLAN.md retained, approved | fixed | unchanged; wrapper adds its own fill check | unchanged | unchanged
readProfile fill after repository.read | PLAN.md proposed, pending | proposed | fill admitted only if no committed write for key since read began; otherwise skip fill, return value | unchanged | unchanged
writeProfile: await write, cache.delete, return | PLAN.md proposed, pending | proposed | unchanged, plus per-key committed-write marker advanced before cache.delete | unchanged | write path also bypasses cache reads (no gain)
Telemetry for added branch | author requirement, approved | n/a | stale-fill-suppressed count on current dashboard, no key labels | none | none
Deterministic regression scenarios | author requirement, approved | required | both completion orders, missing-record creation, overlapping writes, rejected read/write, instance change | not satisfiable | not satisfiable
Acceptance targets 60% / <50% CPU / <60 ms | PLAN.md, approved | fixed | unchanged | unchanged | unchanged
```

Question: D1 — R1: Fix the stale cache fill that breaks read-after-write consistency?
Project/branch/task: main, PLAN.md profile-summary cache wrapper, HOLD SCOPE review.
ELI10: A read can start, a write can finish and clear the cache, then the slow old read
lands and stores the old value. Everyone then sees the old profile for up to 30 seconds,
which the plan explicitly promises cannot happen. Stakes if we pick wrong: correctness SLO
breach that the rollout alert may not catch, or a quietly weakened promise.
Recommendation: A because it is the only option that keeps the retained consistency rule
and is feasible in one event loop with synchronous cache operations (small diff, low
maintenance: one per-key marker checked at fill time).
Completeness: A=10/10, B=3/10, C=3/10
Net: trade a small fill-time check and one counter for keeping the promise the plan already makes.
Header: Stale fill fix
A) Add fill-admission guarantee (recommended)
Amend the wrapper: a fill is admitted only if no repository.write for that key committed since the read began; writeProfile advances that per-key marker before cache.delete. Effort S, risk low, reuses adapter and single-flight unchanged, verification covers both completion orders, missing-record creation, overlapping writes, rejected read/write and instance change. ✅ Keeps "every read after write completes sees the committed version" with no TTL reliance. ✅ Deterministic in the single JS event loop; sync cache ops make the check atomic. ❌ One more per-key in-process state and a new suppressed-fill telemetry branch to test.
B) Keep ordering, allow TTL-bounded staleness
Leave readProfile/writeProfile as proposed and rewrite the consistency contract to allow up to 30 s (10 s absent) staleness after a completed write. Effort S, risk high, no reuse change, verification cannot prove read-after-write. ✅ Zero wrapper changes beyond the proposed code. ✅ Simplest code path to reason about for hit-rate measurement. ❌ Changes a retained consistency requirement, which the author has not authorized.
C) Keep ordering, bypass cache on the write path only
writeProfile skips the cache entirely except for the delete; reads unchanged. Effort S, risk high, no reuse change, verification still fails the stale-fill scenario. ✅ No change to the read path the rollout measures. ✅ Preserves the stated adapter limits and TTLs. ❌ Does not address the race; the stale fill comes from the read path, so the retained rule stays violated.

### 0E. Mode
Mode: HOLD SCOPE; explicit user instruction ("Hold the current scope (HOLD SCOPE mode)").
No mode question asked or logged; mode handoff script unavailable in this fixture (skipped
per run rules). Approved decisions: R1 (D1 → A, scope above). No other approach decision
was needed: the current plan is the only candidate approach and HOLD SCOPE forbids expansion.

### 0G. HOLD SCOPE checks
1. Complexity: estimated 2–3 changed files (wrapper module, wrapper tests, dashboard
   panel config), 0 new classes/services → under the 8-file / 2-class threshold. OK.
2. Minimum change: the two wrapper functions plus the D1 guard. Nothing deferrable
   without blocking the acceptance targets; no deferral proposed, no defer/keep question.
3. Invariants kept: all retained contracts, limits (1000 / 16 MiB / 30 s / 10 s), targets
   (60% / <50% / <60 ms) unchanged. D1 is the one repair needed to meet them.

### 0I. Temporal Interrogation
```
HOUR 1   foundations: adapter API (get/set/delete, absent sentinel), single-flight cohort
         rule, controller instance lifecycle, telemetry counter API. All fixture facts.
HOUR 2-3 core logic: fill-admission guard (D1). Ambiguity: where the per-key marker lives
         and how it is bounded (engineering; see Section 7 requirement). Marker advances
         after repository.write resolves and before cache.delete, synchronously.
HOUR 4-5 integration: controller swap mid-read (old read must not fill new instance,
         already a controller contract); adapter failure mid-write (bypass until reinit).
HOUR 6+  tests: six D1 scenarios with pause/release points; TTL tests on the harness's
         controlled clock, never wall-clock sleeps.
```
Effort: human ~2 days / CC+gstack ~40 min. Feasibility blockers: none after D1.
Pending (engineering, non-blocking): marker data structure and bounding strategy.

## Review Sections (HOLD SCOPE, implementation-ready)

Current scope: mode HOLD SCOPE (explicit instruction). Governing rows: R1 approved
(D1 → A, authority and scope in the ledger). Accepted: plan as written plus the D1
amendment. Deferred: none. Rejected: D1 options B and C. Pending: none blocking.

### Section 1: Architecture Review
```
  caller ──auth/authz──▶ readProfile/writeProfile (wrapper, NEW)
                              │            │
                    cache.get/set/delete   await repository.read/write
                              ▼            ▼
                   existing LRU adapter   existing repository (+ single-flight)
                   (1000 / 16 MiB / 30 s)        │
                                          in-process transactional store
  rollout controller ──publishes──▶ wrapper+cache instance (fresh cohort per change)
```
- Boundaries: wrapper is the only new component; it depends on adapter and repository
  only. New coupling: wrapper↔adapter sentinel semantics (already adapter-owned). Justified.
- Data flow paths: happy (miss→read→fill→return), nil (absent DTO → sentinel 10 s),
  empty (no empty-value shape exists; DTO is always a full object), error (read rejects →
  typed error, no fill). Diagrammed in Section 4.
- State machine (per key, per instance): `empty → filled(v) | absent-sentinel` via
  admitted fill; `any → empty` via cache.delete, TTL expiry, eviction, adapter bypass
  reinit. Invalid transition prevented by D1: `empty → filled(stale)` after a completed
  write; the guard blocks it. Section 4 shows the schedule.
- Scaling: 10x load → hit rate rises, DB load falls; 100x → event-loop CPU on cache ops
  and the 16 MiB cap drive evictions; hit rate falls toward baseline but correctness holds.
- SPOF: the single process (pre-existing). Security: no new surface (Section 3).
- Production failure: adapter throws mid-set → bypass until reinit, DB absorbs load
  (cold-start capacity stated). Rollback: disable flag, instant, controller swaps instance.
**Finding F1 — CRITICAL GAP (resolved):** stale fill after completed write; evidence
trace and remedy under ledger R1 / D1 → A. Residual: marker bounding (Section 7).
Decision gate: F1 resolved by D1 → A; applied to plan. No other findings.

### Section 2: Error & Rescue Map
```
  METHOD/CODEPATH          | WHAT CAN GO WRONG                        | EXCEPTION CLASS
  -------------------------|------------------------------------------|---------------------
  readProfile cache.get    | adapter failure                          | AdapterError (internal)
  readProfile repo.read    | store error / timeout / not found        | existing typed API errors; absent DTO (not an error)
  readProfile cache.set    | adapter failure; byte cap exceeded       | AdapterError (internal)
  readProfile fill guard   | marker says write committed since start  | none (branch, not error)
  writeProfile repo.write  | validation / conflict / store error      | existing typed API errors (rolled back)
  writeProfile cache.delete| adapter failure                          | AdapterError (internal)
  startup                  | multi-process config with caching on     | StartupConfigError (existing)
  -------------------------|------------------------------------------|---------------------
  EXCEPTION CLASS          | RESCUED? | RESCUE ACTION                          | USER SEES
  -------------------------|----------|----------------------------------------|----------------
  AdapterError (get/set)   | Y adapter| bypass cache until empty reinit; count | normal response, slower
  AdapterError (delete)    | Y adapter| bypass until reinit (cache emptied)    | write succeeds
  typed read error         | Y repo   | existing mapping; no fill; cohort freed| existing error
  typed write error        | Y repo   | rollback; no delete; marker unchanged  | existing error
  fill-guard branch        | n/a      | skip fill, return value, count suppressed | fresh value
  StartupConfigError       | Y        | refuse to start                        | deploy fails loudly
```
No catch-alls introduced; wrapper adds no try/catch of its own. No GAPs. Decision gate: no issues found beyond F1 (already resolved).

### Section 3: Security & Threat Model
No new endpoint, input, job or dependency. Keys carry authenticated tenant + validated
profile ID (fixture); cross-tenant hit impossible without key collision, which the key
contract excludes. Values immutable DTOs → no shared-mutation leak. Secrets/keys never
logged; the D1 counter carries no key labels. Threats: cache poisoning via stale fill
(Low likelihood, Med impact) mitigated by D1; memory exhaustion via many keys (Low/Low)
mitigated by 1000 / 16 MiB caps. Decision gate: no issues found.

### Section 4: Data Flow & Interaction Edge Cases
```
INPUT(key) -> VALIDATION(upstream auth/authz, key encoding) -> cache.get
  -> hit: OUTPUT(dto)                     -> miss: repository.read -> fill guard -> cache.set -> OUTPUT
shadow: nil record -> absent DTO -> sentinel 10 s      wrong type -> rejected upstream (existing)
        read rejects -> typed error, no fill            adapter throws -> bypass, OUTPUT from repo
        oversize value -> adapter refuses set, OUTPUT ok   stale (write raced) -> guard suppresses fill
```
Async ordering, invariant: "every read begun after writeProfile fulfills observes the
committed version" (boundary: readProfile invocation vs. writeProfile fulfilment).
```
  readProfile R1        | writeProfile W         | cache(k)      | marker(k)
  get miss; read starts |                        | empty         | g0
                        | write commits v2       | empty         | g0
                        | marker -> g1; delete   | empty         | g1   == W fulfils
  (R2 begins: miss, reads v2, fills v2 if marker still g1)
  read resolves v1      |                        |               |
  guard: g0 != g1 -> skip fill, return v1 to R1's caller (allowed: R1 overlapped W)
```
Order 2 (R1 resolves before W commits): fill v1 admitted at g0; W then deletes it;
later reads miss and read v2. Both orders satisfy the invariant with D1; without D1
order 1 violates it (Step 0 trace). Missing-record creation: same schedule with absent
DTO; guard suppresses the sentinel fill. Overlapping writes W1, W2: marker advances twice;
any read started before either commit is suppressed. Instance change: controller
contract isolates old reads from the new instance. Regression proof: the six D1 scenarios.
Interaction edge cases: no user-visible interaction (backend only). Decision gate: F1
covered by D1 → A; no new issues.

### Section 5: Code Quality Review
Wrapper matches the existing read-through repository pattern; no duplicated behavior
(sentinel handling stays in the adapter, coalescing in the repository). Naming: the
marker should be named for what it means (committed-write generation), engineering's
call. readProfile branches ≤ 4 after D1; writeProfile ≤ 2. No over-engineering; the
original proposal was under-engineered on the race (F1). Decision gate: no new issues.

### Section 6: Test Review
```
  NEW THING                      | TYPE        | HAPPY                 | FAILURE                 | EDGE
  readProfile hit/miss/fill      | unit        | miss→fill→hit         | read rejects → no fill  | absent DTO → sentinel
  fill guard (D1)                | unit        | order 2 admits fill   | order 1 suppresses      | overlapping writes
  writeProfile delete + marker   | unit        | commit→marker→delete  | reject → cache kept     | delete adapter failure
  eviction / byte cap / TTL      | unit        | within caps           | oversize refused        | 1000th/1001st entry
  adapter-failure fallback       | integration | bypass → repo read    | reinit → empty cache    | failure mid-write
  concurrent-miss coalescing     | integration | one store read        | failure releases cohort | fresh cohort after write
  controller instance change     | integration | old writer/new reader | mid-read swap           | predicate parity
  suppressed-fill counter        | unit        | increments once       | no key label present    | zero when no race
```
Assertion check: each row maps to a retained contract or the D1 remedy; the D1 rows assert
the exact committed version observed by the post-write read, not a lower bound. 2am test:
D1 scenario (a). Hostile QA: overlapping writes + absent record + instance swap in one
schedule. Chaos: adapter throwing on every call under load. Pyramid: unit-heavy, correct.
Flakiness: TTL and ordering tests must use the harness's controlled clock and pause/release
points, never timers. Load test: existing rollout stages serve as the load check.
Decision gate: coverage already approved by author requirements and D1; no new question.

### Section 7: Performance Review
No N+1, no new queries or indexes, no new connections. Memory: cache ≤ 16 MiB (adapter).
**WARNING W1:** the D1 per-key marker is new in-process state; it must stay bounded (for
example retained only while a read for that key is in flight, or capped alongside the
cache). Requirement recorded; data structure left to engineering; verification: a test
that marker state is released after reads complete. Slow paths: miss path = existing
read + two sync cache ops; hit path sub-millisecond. Decision gate: W1 is a required
property of the approved remedy, not a new choice; recorded for engineering.

### Section 8: Observability & Debuggability Review
Existing metrics (hit/miss, eviction, bytes, fallback, DB CPU, p95) plus the D1
suppressed-fill counter on the current dashboard, no key labels. Alerts: existing set
(SLO breach, p95 > 120 ms 5 min, bypass > 1 min); none added per author. Debuggability:
a stale-read report 3 weeks later is reconstructible from suppressed-fill and bypass
counts plus the flag-stage timeline in the runbook. Decision gate: no issues found.

### Section 9: Deployment & Rollout Review
No migration. Flag staged 10% → 50% → 100% with one healthy hour each; criteria as
stated. Rollback: disable flag → controller drains writes, publishes bypass instance;
seconds. Risk window: single process, no old/new code overlap. Post-deploy: first 5 min
watch bypass and error rate; first hour watch hit rate and p95. Smoke: one read-after-
write probe on a synthetic tenant. Decision gate: no issues found.

### Section 10: Long-Term Trajectory Review
Debt: marker state needs a short ASCII comment (schedule diagram above) in the wrapper.
Path dependency: none; the repository interface stays the replacement seam. Reversibility
5/5. Ecosystem fit: reuses adapter, single-flight, controller. 1-year question: obvious
if the comment and the six scenarios ship. Decision gate: no issues found.

### Section 11: Design & UX Review
SKIPPED (no UI scope).
